subject: Pilot readiness: SDK onboarding + JSON resilience checklist
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot readiness: SDK onboarding + JSON resilience checklist

Thanks again for the call today — great discussion and lots of alignment on the pilot goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we don’t lose momentum: 

Key outcomes from discovery:
- Target workflows: user-facing recommendation enrichment and a nightly rerank job (low-latency for recommendations, batch for rerank).
- Infra: you’re running EKS in us-west with internal identity via OIDC (Auth0).
- Success metrics: P95 latency < 350ms for recommendations, JSON schema pass rate > 99.5% for structured outputs, embedding similarity AUC > 0.78 for reranker tests.

Technical asks (we need confirmations from your side):
1) Auth mode for pilot endpoints (OIDC client id/redirects or API key with IP restrictions?).
2) Allowed egress destinations for embeddings (we currently call internal embedding replicas — confirm vendor constraints).
3) Any strict JSON schema fields that must always be present vs optional? (examples: item_id, score, metadata).
4) Retry policy tolerance: how many soft-fail retries acceptable before falling back to plain-text response?

Proposed Redwood deliverables for the pilot:
- SDK onboarding package (node/python): quickstart + sample request/response for constrained decoding.
- JSON validation runbook: schema, constrained-decoder config, post-validation retry flow.
- Mutual action plan (attached) with milestones: env access, SDK integration, embedding/reranker validation, pilot kickoff.

Please see the attached MAP draft and security questionnaire request. Can you confirm the auth approach and share a point of contact for procurement? If you’re ok, I’ll schedule a tech deep-dive next week to align on schema fields and retry timeline.

Thanks,

Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot readiness: SDK onboarding + JSON resilience checklist

Thanks for the concise recap, Aditya — appreciated. A few clarifications and answers inline: 

- Auth: We prefer OIDC for the pilot. We can stand up a client ID/secret for Redwood and restrict to your redirect URIs. I’ll connect you to our SRE for the callbacks.
- Egress: embeddings must stay inside our VPC; we’ll provide a VPC endpoint for API calls. Vendor for embeddings is internal (homegrown vector service) — we can provide an endpoint and auth token once procurement signs NDA.
- JSON schema: must include item_id (string), score (float), source (enum), and metadata (object) — metadata can be sparse but the top-level keys must exist.
- Retry: For user-facing recs we can tolerate up to 2 retries with exponential backoff; after that fallback to last-known-good ranked list. For batch rerank jobs we can retry longer (10m window).

Attaching our security questionnaire and the procurement contact information. Happy to do the technical deep-dive. Samir and I are available Tue/Wed afternoon PT.

—Jamie
Jamie Liao
Head of Product, Finlytics
jamie@finlytics.ai

Attachments: Finlytics-Security-Questionnaire.pdf (pdf)

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Jamie — that auth/egress guidance is helpful. Below is a proposed technical plan for the pilot SDK + JSON resilience that maps to your constraints. If this looks good I’ll share the SDK quickstart and schedule the tech deep-dive (30–45m) to walk through the schema and test harness.

1) SDK onboarding (deliver in two weeks)- Deliverables: redwood-python and redwood-node quickstart repos, example integration with OIDC client flow, sample env variables for VPC endpoint.- Goal: successful generate/embeddings calls from a dev environment behind your VPC endpoint.

2) Structured output constraints (constrained decoding + schema)- Approach: use token-level constraints where possible and a two-step validation pipeline: a) constrained-decode with a hardened token whitelist for required keys, b) post-hoc JSON schema validation (fast local validator).- If schema validation fails, we apply a single automated retry with adjusted decoding temperature and a stronger whitelist; if the retry also fails we surface a deterministic fallback payload (last-known-good or a minimal schema response) and log the incident to the pilot dashboard.

3) Validation + retry patterns- User-facing: 1 retry (exponential backoff), fallback to last-known-good. Send telemetry event for every schema failure.- Batch rerank: configurable retry window up to 10m with backoff and alerting to Finlytics SRE if >5% of job items fail validation.

4) Embeddings / reranker validation- Plan: sandbox 1k sample items from Finlytics for offline A/B with your current reranker. We’ll provide tooling to compute similarity AUC and a small dashboard.

5) Routing & region considerations- Default: route to us-west region for pilot. If you need multi-region failover we can add a read-only replica in eu-west as a follow-up.

Acceptance criteria (for pilot success):
- SDK integration completed (dev-to-dev calls)
- JSON schema pass rate >= 99.5% for user-facing calls
- Embedding/reranker AUC delta within agreed threshold (>0.78)

Next steps (proposed):
- Confirm OIDC client creation and SRE contact (you)
- Procurement to confirm NDA and sandbox data share (Samir / procurement)
- Tech deep-dive: proposed slots Tue 5/11 3:00pm PT or Wed 5/12 2:00pm PT

I’ve attached the SDK quickstart and the JSON validation runbook for your review. Also linking the MAP we shared earlier: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-FinlyticsPilot

If you confirm the auth approach and pick a deep-dive slot I’ll lock it in.

Thanks,

Aditya Rao
